content:
rachel: Noticed a weird flurry of duplicate webhook deliveries from the onboarding sampleapp this morning. Pattern: createWebhook -> 429 -> client retries with very small fixed jitter (30ms) -> auth refresh completes between retry attempts -> server accepts duplicate.

rachel: quick log snippet: 
```
2026-03-18T08:03:21Z INFO req=wx-112 status=429 backoff=30ms
2026-03-18T08:03:21Z INFO auth=refresh start for session=s-99
2026-03-18T08:03:21Z INFO retry req=wx-112 headers=(authorization: Bearer newtok) // missing x-rw-replay-id
2026-03-18T08:03:21Z INFO server created webhook id=hook-501 duplicate=true
```

diego: ugh. Is this different from the other "replay id lost on refresh" threads or a new variant?

priya: seems related but got me thinking about multi-chunk/streaming operations where we need sequence numbers. For webhooks it's a single logical call, but we still need to guarantee that the replay-id persists across refreshes and retry clones.

nathan: two independent angles: (1) jitter/backoff policy — small fixed jitters are bad when auth refresh windows are deterministic ~40-120ms, (2) header lifecycle — replay id must be owned by the logical request and survive any auth client swap or shallow-clone during retry.

rachel: proposed short-term mitigations: increase sampleapp min 429 backoff to 200ms and add a tutorial note. But long-term we should patch SDKs.

diego: agreed. I propose a compact cross-SDK spec: header x-rw-replay-id (per-logical-request, stable across retries), optional x-rw-replay-seq (seq number for chunked/streamed operations), and a strong recommendation to attach replay-id before any auth/refresh step. Also recommend default 429 backoff: exp backoff with base 100ms and jitter +/-50% (not fixed tiny values).

priya: draft spec snippet: 
```
semantics:
  - x-rw-replay-id: uuidv4 string, generated at API boundary, immutable for logical request lifetime
  - x-rw-replay-seq: integer (optional), starts at 1 for first chunk; server dedups by (replay-id, seq)
SDK guidance:
  - generate replay-id before calling auth.ensureValid()
  - carry replay-id in request-context so token refresh replaces only auth header
  - retry clones must merge meta->headers and preserve replay-id
  - streaming: include seq header for each chunk
```

nathan: sample Node pseudo: 
```js
// at API entry
const replayId = opts.headers['x-rw-replay-id'] || uuid();
req.ctx = { ...(req.ctx||{}), replayId };
req.headers['x-rw-replay-id'] = replayId;
await auth.ensureValid(req.ctx); // may refresh but ctx persists
return transport.send(req);
```

diego: for Go we recommend context.WithValue(ctx, "rw.replay.id", id) and ensure http.Request clones copy context. Also note: avoid storing replay-id on short-lived auth client instances (they get swapped on refresh).

priya: test plan: unit + integration harness that (a) simulates token rotate mid-retry, (b) asserts no duplicate side-effects for create endpoints, and (c) asserts streaming endpoints honor seq semantics. Add CI job that runs the harness in sampleapp matrix.

rachel: ops question: do we want a server-side safeguard too? e.g., accept idempotency header for a short TTL keyed by user+replay-id to protect older clients. That would be a belt-and-suspenders approach.

nathan: server-side TTL is wise; store (user, replay-id) -> last-seq seen and expiry=5m. But primary fix must be SDK parity. We'll document server dedupe semantics in the spec.

diego: rolling plan: (1) land Node patch to attach replay-id at API boundary + clone fixes + tests, (2) mirror to Go/Python via small code snippets and PRs, (3) update sampleapp defaults and onboarding docs, (4) add metric duplicates_per_100k and dashboard, (5) optional server-side TTL for conservative protection.

ops-bot: created card DEVEX-5088: replay-id-spec + SDK parity work -> assigned devex + eng-platform

priya: i'll author the one-page spec and include two minimal code snippets per SDK + a tiny harness repo that can fake auth rotations and assert no duplicate side-effects. Will also include recommended jitter/backoff defaults (exp backoff, base=100ms, max=2s, jitter=0.5).

rachel: thanks. i'll add repro logs to the card and bump sampleapp backoff until SDKs are patched. Please tag me in PR reviews. :thumbsup:
